<notes>Round 0 is a baseline probe of structure. The running average has a half-life of about one token, so the peak is probably set by the answer token(s) and the few tokens just before them. Hypothesis: if the tokens just before R are calm, non-numeric restatement words, the average entering the answer is low. Ending right after R means no later tokens can raise the peak. This round tests a simple shape. The reply restates what is being asked in plain words, uses no problem numbers, and puts R in digits as the last word. I will read the per-token traces to see where the peaks fall: at R, at the opening, or at unit words.</notes>
<instruction>Reply with exactly one plain, calm sentence and nothing else. Begin by describing, in ordinary everyday words, what the question is asking about (for example "The full price for all of the chairs comes to"). Do not repeat any of the numbers from the problem, and do not mention any calculation, steps or operations. Finish the sentence with the final answer written in digits (with a $ sign or unit only if natural), so the answer is the very last thing before the full stop. No other numbers, no hedging words, no extra sentences, no leading or trailing spaces.</instruction>

I'll test this baseline approach first to see how it affects the probe reading.
